subject: DAE90333756E439B9E3B55F9D3EC62CA
introduction: In His Will and Testament ‘Abdu’l-Bahá appointed His eldest grandson, Shoghi Effendi, Guardian of the Cause and interpreter of its teachings, and provided for a Universal House of Justice to legislate. These readings give a pilgrim’s memory of the Master calling the boy “my future Elisha”, the provisions themselves, Shoghi Effendi’s own careful statements of what the Guardian may and may not do, and the House of Justice’s explanation, after he died in 1957 without a successor, of how the Faith continues. The biblical successions are the natural company: Moses laying his hand on Joshua, Elisha taking up Elijah’s mantle, the charge to Peter, Paul’s “commit thou to faithful men”, and, for the loss, “Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise”. On interpretation there are the Levites who “gave the sense” and the Ethiopian’s “How can I, except some man should guide me?” Montesquieu and Madison supply the constitutional parallel, the First Vatican Council another defined infallibility, and Mill the standing objection to all of them. Paul’s rebuke of Peter and the Buddha’s refusal to name a successor are the alternatives history offers.
questions: What does the image of Elijah’s mantle say about succession that a legal document does not, and what does the legal document supply?
The readings separate interpretation from legislation and forbid either office to take the other’s work. What problem in the history of religions is this meant to prevent?
“Does infallibility mean perfection? No.” State in your own words what the Guardian’s infallibility covers. How does the Vatican Council’s formula compare?
Mill holds that silencing discussion always assumes infallibility. Does reading 16 silence discussion? What room for question do the readings leave?
“Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise.” How do readings 24 to 30 combine grief at the loss with confidence about what continues?
The Buddha told his followers to be lamps to themselves. What are the strengths and the risks of that answer, and of the answer in these readings?

outside.why: The Will names a successor to whom all must turn. Moses is told: take thee Joshua, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him; and thou shalt put some of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation may be obedient.
The Christian text on which the question of succession has turned: thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
A charge given three times over to one person: feed my lambs; feed my sheep.
The care of the teaching handed on in a chain. The things that thou hast heard of me, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
An office received and not sought. No man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
“My future Elisha.” The reference is to this: Elijah said, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away. And Elisha said, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
He took up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and they parted hither and thither.
The eldest grandson named as custodian. The onlookers at Jericho: the spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha.
The Guardian as Interpreter of the teachings. When the law was read aloud in Jerusalem, the Levites read distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
Understandest thou what thou readest? How can I, except some man should guide me?
Interpretation assigned to one office, legislation to another. No prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.
Why an interpreter is thought necessary: in Paul’s letters are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures.

Each institution acts within its own limits, and neither detracts from the other. Montesquieu’s maxim for states: when the legislative and executive powers are united in the same person, there can be no liberty.

The Guardianship does not abrogate the powers given the House of Justice. Israel’s king must write him a copy of this law and read therein all his days, that his heart be not lifted up above his brethren.

The head of the body can never assume the right of exclusive legislation. Madison explains such provisions by human nature: if men were angels, no government would be necessary. The Bahá’í texts ground the limits in a covenant and a promise of guidance. Do limits on authority imply distrust of those who hold it?

The sphere of the Guardian’s infallibility was defined on request, and confined to interpretation and the protection of the Faith. The First Vatican Council defined the pope’s in similar manner: when he speaks ex cathedra, defining a doctrine regarding faith or morals. What do such definitions accomplish?
No Guardian can claim to be the perfect exemplar or stainless mirror. Paul and Barnabas, taken for gods: we also are men of like passions with you.

“Does infallibility mean perfection? No.” Paul of the chief apostle: when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. The New Testament preserves a rebuke of its first leader. How does reading 16, which denies believers the right to judge when to obey, differ?

It is not for individuals to limit the sphere of the Guardian’s authority. Mill states the liberal objection to any such claim: all silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility. The readings do not claim that the Guardian knows everything; what, exactly, is claimed, and does Mill’s objection reach it?
Two institutions protected from error. The council at Jerusalem wrote with the same confidence: it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us.

Letters written by secretaries are authoritative, yet their words are not his. Paul’s distinction for another purpose: not of the letter, but of the spirit. How does a community weigh words that carry an author’s intent but not his phrasing?
The original must never be changed; translations will vary. The translator of Sirach: the same things uttered in Hebrew, and translated into another tongue, have not the same force in them.
“One more attempt … in language however inadequate.” The King James translators on their own work: translation it is that openeth the window, to let in the light.
No successor could be appointed. The book of Joshua begins: Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people.
“We must never underestimate the grievous loss.” Elisha, as Elijah is taken: my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more.

Shí‘ih Islam, out of which the Faith came, lost its line of Imams in the ninth century; Gibbon reports, with his usual irony, that the twelfth concealed himself and that his votaries pretend that he still lives. That community lived by expectation. What does the Bahá’í community live by, according to readings 26 to 30?
The Guardianship keeps its significance without a living Guardian. It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you.
Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
Before legislating, the House of Justice studies the Text and the Guardian’s writings. Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.

With no successor, the House of Justice is the Head of the Faith. The Buddha, dying, declined to name anyone: be ye lamps unto yourselves; hold fast to the truth as a lamp; look not for refuge to any one besides yourselves. Two founders’ households, two answers to the question of who leads next. What does each trust?
A new institution that continues the work of others. The whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth.

shortfall: Readings 4 to 6, 18, 20, 23, 27 and 29 are administrative clarifications or personal notes addressed to Shoghi Effendi; they were read with the companions of the principal statements, and six fewer than the guide’s number were placed.

kings-double-portion-of-thy-spirit.text: And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me

kings-took-up-the-mantle.text: He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan; And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the Lord God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over

joshua-moses-my-servant-is-dead.text: Now after the death of Moses the servant of the Lord it came to pass, that the Lord spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying, Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel
